answer: The timber test I would run is Signed neighbourhood watch patrol log: patrols walked with neighbours for three years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that patrols walked with neighbours for three years — so privacy survives, and the knoll is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the grove of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
